## Incident review: checkout payments failing (18 Sep 2026)

**Severity:** SEV-1 · **Duration:** 47 minutes · **Author:** R. Achebe (Nimbus Metrics SRE)

### What happened
At 14:02 UTC, about 38% of card payments at checkout started failing with a timeout. Customers saw "something went wrong" and some retried, which created 112 duplicate charges that we later refunded.

### Timeline
- 14:02 error rate alert fires
- 14:09 on-call identifies the payments gateway pods restarting in a loop
- 14:31 rollback of the 13:55 config deploy
- 14:49 error rate back to baseline

### Root cause
A config change lowered the connection-pool size for the gateway from 200 to 20. Under normal afternoon load the pool was exhausted and health checks timed out, so Kubernetes kept killing healthy pods.

### What went well / what didn't
The alert fired quickly. Rollback took too long because the deploy wasn't tagged.

### Follow-ups
1. Validate pool-size config in CI (owner: platform)
2. Add idempotency keys to the retry path so retries can't double charge (owner: payments)
3. Tag every config deploy (owner: SRE)

This was a blameless review.
